OPEN METHODS / REAL MEASUREMENTS

Useful AI starts
with honest evidence.

A trained CNN, a held-out test set, and a clear boundary between

THE MODEL

Small enough to work
right where you are.

MobileNetV3-Small is a convolutional neural network. Its ImageNet-pretrained feature extractor is frozen; a new six-class linear head is trained on TrashNet material images.

Images are resized to 160 × 160 and normalized with ImageNet channel statistics. Training adds crop, horizontal-flip and colour augmentation. Validation loss selects the checkpoint; the test set is used only for final evaluation.

PER-CLASS PERFORMANCE

Where it works.
Where to look twice.

F1 balances precision and recall. These are in-dataset results, not field performance.

A realistic business hypothesis.

Customer: small recycling collection sites and community waste banks that need consistent intake records and easier staff onboarding.

Offer: assisted material classification with human review and exportable logs. This working pilot is free. A future team edition could add shared records and site-specific acceptance rules.

Price to test: IDR 199,000 per site/month. This is a proposal, not a validated price or an active subscription.

Pilot: test with 3 sites for 4 weeks. Compare sorting time, correction rate and contamination against their existing process. Proceed only if measured benefit exceeds the operating cost.

Know the boundaries.

  • TrashNet uses mostly single objects on a plain background. Real collection floors are harder.
  • This model always scores one of six classes. It cannot reliably reject unfamiliar or hazardous objects.
  • Softmax scores are uncalibrated; a high score can still be wrong.
  • No plastic-resin identification, contamination detection, or local recycling-rule verification.
  • Human review is required. Batteries, chemicals, sharps and medical waste need specialist handling.

Data: TrashNet, Gary Thung & Mindy Yang. CNN: Torchvision MobileNetV3. Runtime: ONNX Runtime Web.
